correctness.rationale: For T=conv{(1,0),(-1/2,±sqrt(3)/2)}, Q_r={|x|+|y|<=r}, all r>0 and planar translations, horizontal sections give symmetric triangle halfwidth A=(1-x)/sqrt(3) and diamond halfwidth B=r-|x-t|; vertical displacement cannot increase overlap. Square-in-triangle and triangle-in-diamond vertex inequalities yield r_-=3(sqrt(3)-1)/4 and r_+=(3+sqrt(3))/4 and the 2r² and 3sqrt(3)/4 plateaus (including boundaries). At t_*=(1+2r(1-sqrt(3)))/4 for each strict intermediate r, all six section breakpoint inequalities hold; exact symbolic integration of the three clipped pieces was independently recomputed to I_r(t)=3sqrt(3)/4-sqrt(3)(r_+-r)^2-2(t-t_*)² locally. Brunn--Minkowski gives concavity of sqrt I_r on the connected positive-overlap translation interval; an interior stationary point is globally maximizing and local strict concavity precludes a second horizontal optimizer. At each positive-length switch point of the halfwidth functions, any nonzero vertical displacement strictly loses positive area, giving unique planar optimum (t_*,0). Exact checks established continuity at both thresholds and the r=1 center overlap 2sqrt(3)-9/4, maximum 3/8+sqrt(3)/2, ratio (82-40sqrt(3))/13, and gap 21/8-3sqrt(3)/2. Independent Shapely planar clipping with numerical optimizers across 11 radii corroborated the expression; those finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete exact one-parameter translative overlap classification for two canonical regular polygons of incompatible rotational symmetry solves a natural shape-matching problem rather than an arbitrary numeric instance. The sharp transitions correspond to full containment versus genuine partial contact; the unique intermediate optimizer supplies geometric rigidity; the exactly quantified centroid-alignment loss is a useful concrete benchmark beyond generic algorithmic solvability or universal bounds. A researcher studying fixed-orientation cross-covariograms or convex overlap can use the precise phase cutoffs and optimizers without recomputing the polygon geometry.
